**Beta-Blockers** ★★ — Competitive β antagonists (↓cAMP/Ca²⁺ → ↓HR, ↓contractility, ↓AV conduction, ↓renin): pick subclass by receptor selectivity, avoid unopposed α₁ and bronchospasm.

- **Typical case:** Chronic HFrEF (euvolaemic) → bisoprolol, carvedilol, or metoprolol succinate ↓mortality ★★; overdose → refractory bradycardia + hypotension + hypoglycaemia → **IV glucagon** ★★.

## Subclasses (vs)

| Subclass | Drugs | Key effect | Distinguishing trap / niche |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cardioselective β₁** ★ | Metoprolol, bisoprolol, atenolol, **esmolol** | ↓HR, ↓contractility, ↓renin; spares β₂ | Selectivity ==lost at high doses==; esmolol t½ ==9 min== |
| **Non-selective β₁ + β₂** | **Propranolol**, nadolol, timolol | + blocks β₂ bronchodilation & glycogenolysis | ==Avoid in asthma==; propranolol: tremor, migraine, thyroid storm (↓T4→T3), varices |
| **Mixed α₁ + β** | **Carvedilol**, **labetalol** | Adds α₁ vasodilation (↓afterload) | Labetalol IV: hypertensive emergency / aortic dissection |
| **Partial agonist (ISA)** | Pindolol, acebutolol | Less resting bradycardia | Lower intrinsic suppression at rest |

## Numbers & key rules

| Item | Value / Rule | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Esmolol half-life | ==9 minutes== | Acute perioperative rate / dissection control |
| Withdrawal taper | ==1 to 2 weeks== | Prevents rebound tachycardia & angina (β-receptor upregulation) |
| Bradycardia cut-off | HR ==<50 bpm== (symptomatic) | Contraindication |

## High-yield uses & adverse effects

- **HFrEF mortality benefit** ★★: bisoprolol, carvedilol, metoprolol succinate — start ==once euvolaemic==, ==never in acute decompensated shock==.
- **Diabetes trap** ★★: masks tremor/palpitations of hypoglycaemia; **diaphoresis persists** (cholinergic).
- **Overdose** ★★: **IV glucagon** (activates adenylyl cyclase independent of β receptors) + atropine + high-dose insulin euglycaemia.

## ⚠ Never

- ==Do not give== in 2nd/3rd-degree AV block ==without a pacemaker==, symptomatic bradycardia ==<50 bpm==, cardiogenic shock, or overt decompensated HF.
- ==Avoid non-selective agents in asthma== (severe bronchospasm).
- ==Never== give pure β-blocker in cocaine toxicity or untreated phaeochromocytoma (unopposed α₁ vasoconstriction) ★★.
- ==Never== stop abruptly (taper over ==1 to 2 weeks==).

## Buzzword →

- **Unopposed alpha-1 vasoconstriction** → pure β-blocker in cocaine toxicity or untreated phaeochromocytoma
- **Diaphoresis persists in hypoglycaemia** → β-blockers mask adrenergic signs but not cholinergic sweating
- **Ultra-short t½ 9 min** → esmolol
- **Refractory bradycardia + IV glucagon** → β-blocker overdose

## Cards

- Which three beta-blockers reduce mortality in chronic HFrEF and when are they started? → Bisoprolol, carvedilol, and metoprolol succinate; start only once euvolaemic, never in acute decompensated shock
- Does beta-1 cardioselectivity hold at all doses? → No; selectivity is lost at high doses
- Why does sweating persist during hypoglycaemia on beta-blockers? → Beta-blockers mask adrenergic signs (tremor, palpitations), whereas diaphoresis is cholinergic
- Why are pure beta-blockers dangerous in cocaine toxicity or untreated phaeochromocytoma? → They cause unopposed alpha-1 vasoconstriction and severe hypertension
- First-line antidote for beta-blocker overdose and its mechanism → IV glucagon; activates adenylyl cyclase independently of beta receptors (plus atropine and high-dose insulin)
- Absolute cardiac contraindications to beta-blockers → 2nd/3rd-degree AV block without a pacemaker, severe symptomatic bradycardia (<50 bpm), cardiogenic shock, and overt decompensated HF
- How should chronic beta-blockers be discontinued? → Taper over 1 to 2 weeks to prevent rebound tachycardia and angina
